newsitem.title: USA: Judge orders witness-list swap in tobacco trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge orders witness-list swap in tobacco trial.

text.p: A Florida judge on Monday ordered rival lawyers to exchange witness lists in a class-action suit for non-smoking flight attendants allegedly made sick by second-hand smoke.

The order by Dade County Circuit Court Judge Robert Kaye settled a long dispute between lawyers preparing for a scheduled June 2 trial, which is the first class-action suit against tobacco companies likely to be heard by a jury.

Other class action suits on behalf of sick smokers are also making their ways through U.S. courts, part of a wave of anti-tobacco litigation seen as a serious court threat to the rich industry after decades of failed smoker lawsuits.
Stanley and Susan Rosenblatt, the husband and wife team bringing the flight-attendants suit, must hand over lists of expert and other witnesses by March 2.

A month later, after tobacco-company lawyers have examined their list, the names of witnesses scheduled to testify for Philip Morris Cos Inc, RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp and other cigarette makers will be given to the Rosenblatts.

Each side will be allowed to question opposing witnesses before trial, which will turn on whether or not second-hand smoke causes illnessess and if tobacco companies hid knowledge of any dangers from the public.

The Rosenblatts argued that the exchange of witnesses should be simultaneous, but tobacco company lawyers, including Ed Moss for the Brown & Williamson unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, said a two-step exchange was needed. Otherwise, each side's witness lists would contain hundreds of names.
"When we learn what witnesses and what issues they intend to present at trial, we can respond meaningfully," Moss said.
